name: cache-keepalive
description: Keeps the main thread's prompt cache warm while you are idle: one cheap fork ping just before the TTL runs out, capped, verified on every hit.

leadMinutes.title: Minutes before expiry to ping
leadMinutes.description: Ping this many minutes before the cache TTL runs out

compactLeadMinutes.title: Minutes before expiry to compact
compactLeadMinutes.description: An armed compact starts this many minutes before the cache TTL runs out. Longer ahead than a ping, since compacting a big context takes minutes (about 1 min at 140k tokens)

maxPings.title: Pings per idle stretch
maxPings.description: Default cap on pings while idle; /keepalive brb raises it once

minContextTokens.title: Minimum context to keep warm
minContextTokens.description: Below this many context tokens a rewrite is cheap, so no pings

engineStatus.title: Show state under the prompt
engineStatus.description: For sessions without a custom status line: pin the keepalive state as a Claude Code status entry (drawn on its own row with a warning-style prefix)

telegramBotToken.title: Telegram bot token
telegramBotToken.description: Bot that asks whether to keep the cache warm once the pings run out. Also read from CLAUDE_KEEPALIVE_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN or the macOS Keychain item 'claude-code.cache-keepalive' (account 'telegram-bot-token'). Empty: no Telegram

telegramChatId.title: Telegram chat ID
telegramChatId.description: Chat that receives the question, e.g. the group session-notifier posts to

telegramUserId.title: Telegram user ID
telegramUserId.description: Only this user's button presses and replies count. Empty: anyone in the chat

compactBeforeExpiry.title: Compact before the cache expires
compactBeforeExpiry.description: Every idle stretch, once the pings are used up, compact in the lead window before expiry while the cache is still warm, so the summary request reads it. Off by default: it changes your context. /keepalive compact arms it for one stretch instead
